newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PALESTINIAN SHARES UP AS NEW COMPANY ENTERS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PALESTINIAN SHARES UP AS NEW COMPANY ENTERS MARKET.

text.p: The Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) closed up on Wednesday as a 16th company entered the market, a PSE statement said.
The Jerusalem Index rose 2.36 to 104.63, the largest increase since the PSE started issuing its index on July 13.
The statement also said 140,379 shares worth 226,368 Jordanian dinars changed hands, up from 134,713 shares valued at 204,807 dinars which were traded on Sunday.
Palestinian shares are traded twice weekly, on Sundays and Wednesdays.
PSE General Manager Safwan Bataineh said in the statement the rise was due in part to the addition of a new company, the Jerusalem Cigarette Company (JCC).
He said shares in that company rose 10 percent to 4.95 dinars per share and accounted for slightly more than two percent of the day's trade.
The basic price for JCC was established by an odd lot trade of 38 shares last Sunday at a price of 4.50 dinars, he said.
The PSE on Wednesday also began floating share prices subject to a two percent ceiling on upward and downward price movements.
"(This) is expected to result in increased volatility in both the index and share prices," the statement said.
In trading on Wednesday, the Palestine Telecommunications Company, which accounted for 81 percent of the trade volume, rose two percent to 1.53 dinars per share.
Shares in seven other companies traded even.
Trading is conducted in dollars or Jordanian dinars in absence of a Palestinian currency.
